cards.title: Structural reforms
cards.author: Editorial
cards.why: Provides critical official economic data and policy arguments for CSS Economy, Governance, and Essay papers.
cards.summary: The State Bank of Pakistan's latest annual report warns that recent macroeconomic stabilization is insufficient without fundamental structural reforms. Factors such as early deindustrialisation, policy unpredictability, and low investment continue to limit employment and output. In addition, low female participation and an undertrained youth workforce restrict productive capacity across the economy. Sustainable expansion requires policy continuity across successive administrations alongside tax administrative reform.
key_facts: According to the State Bank of Pakistan, national unemployment increased to 7.2% in 2025 compared to 5.7% in 2018.
The central bank identified premature deindustrialisation, deficient investment, low skill levels, and widespread informal work as main hurdles to growth.
The SBP report underscored that policy reversals and lack of continuity across governments severely impede private and foreign investment.

vocab.meaning: the decline of industrial capacity or manufacturing activity in an economy
capable of withstanding shocks or recovering quickly

text: THE country’s improving macroeconomic health offers little hope when growth remains too weak to create enough jobs or improve living standards. The State Bank’s latest annual report makes this contradiction difficult to ignore. It argues that structural reforms are essential for putting the economy on a sustainable high-growth path. The figures underline the scale of the problem. The SBP has correctly identified premature deindustrialisation, weak investment, inadequate skills and widespread informal employment as major constraints. These problems have accumulated over decades of inconsistent economic policies. The state’s reform priorities must therefore address the reasons businesses hesitate to invest and expand.

Infrastructure gaps require attention. Tax administration needs simplification, with a broader tax base. Businesses also need predictable regulations and consistent policies. Repeated policy reversals have made long-term planning difficult for domestic and foreign investors alike. The domestic labour market presents an equally serious challenge. While overall unemployment has risen to 7.2pc in 2025 from 5.7pc in 2018, low female workforce participation keeps a substantial share of potential workers outside productive economic activity. High youth unemployment reflects weaknesses in education and vocational training. Universities and technical institutions must develop skills that employers actually need. The agricultural sector needs modern irrigation, better technology and climate-resilient practices. However, the most important lesson from the SBP report concerns policy continuity. Structural reforms cannot succeed through isolated announcements or short-lived initiatives. They require political commitment across successive governments. Every change in administration should not bring another round of economic experimentation. The government must recognise that sustainable growth requires a stronger productive base. Without consistent investment, industrial expansion, better skills and higher productivity, economic stability will remain vulnerable. The real test of reform will be whether it creates productive jobs and raises household incomes.

cards.title: Anti-rape action
cards.author: Editorial
cards.why: Supplies precise official statistics and legal references for questions on Gender Studies, Human Rights, and Criminal Justice.
cards.summary: The Punjab government has announced plans for a new anti-rape law and fast-track courts to resolve cases of violence against women and children within set deadlines. Even so, patriarchal norms, official reluctance, and forced out-of-court settlements continue to foster impunity for sexual crimes. While legal frameworks like the Anti-Rape Act of 2021 exist, the real shortfall lies in weak implementation and inadequate forensic infrastructure. Raising conviction rates requires modern DNA testing capabilities, specialised investigations, and social awareness led by female representatives.
key_facts: Punjab police stations registered 1.24 million complaints regarding females, according to the provincial police chief.
The Women Virtual Police Station in Punjab alone received approximately 125,000 complaints.
Police data indicated that 71% of sexual abuse perpetrators were individuals already known to their victims.
The Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act was passed in 2021 to ensure rapid trials and specialized inquiries into sexual violence.

vocab.meaning: relating to a social structure dominated by men
freedom from punishment or exemption from the consequences of a crime

text: THE prevalence of rape in Pakistan means it can be a dangerous place for females. Yet, the issue is left out of political agendas. The Punjab government’s plan to introduce an anti-rape law, and establish fast-track courts to expedite the trials of violence against women and children cases with a definite timeframe for their disposal, is welcome. The problem, however, is more complex. On one end are patriarchal social structures that condone crimes of power, and on the other, is the absence of official and judicial resolve. Resultantly, the high numbers are a reality check for the government and its claims about preventive actions. As per the provincial police chief, police stations across Punjab logged 1.24m complaints related to females. The Women Virtual Police Station alone recorded nearly 125,000, while 71pc of sexual abuse offenders were known to their victims.

There is no dearth of laws. The state has long failed in carrying out its duty to enforce them, and foster a setting where women’s safety matters. The Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act, 2021 is in place for the speedy investigation and trial of rape and sexual violence cases involving women and children. The Punjab government can adopt its provisions as modern forensic and medico-legal departments, DNA testing, alongside a sensitised police force are important. Meanwhile, victim-blaming, and out-of-court settlements, often attained through coercion, feed rape impunity. The burden of shame is for the perpetrator to bear. For better conviction rates, attitudes must change. Women politicians must play a greater role in raising awareness in conservative areas to ensure offences are reported, penalties known, and laws implemented. Additionally, countrywide training for specialised probes to secure convictions cannot be delayed. Rape scars for life. A pro-survivor response alongside pre-emptive measures should be central to Pakistan’s criminal justice policy. When rape happens so frequently, justice is the sole safeguard for women’s respect.

cards.title: Hardening lines
cards.author: Editorial
cards.why: Relevant for questions on federalism, administrative restructuring, and coalition governance in Pakistan Affairs.
cards.summary: Tensions have surfaced within the ruling coalition regarding proposals to create new administrative provinces. Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari warned that imposing provincial divisions by force could cause unrest, advocating instead for political dialogue and respecting the opposition's mandate. In contrast, several federal ministers have publicly pushed for a nationwide referendum on the subject. This dispute underscores how major constitutional debates are being argued through the press rather than resolved inside the cabinet.
key_facts: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari argued at the Karachi Press Club that referendums in Pakistan's history have historically served undemocratic purposes.
Ministers within the ruling coalition, primarily from the PML-N, have publicly proposed holding a nationwide referendum on carving out new provinces.
The PPP leadership disclosed that the prime minister and federal cabinet members had not formally discussed the new provinces initiative with the president before speaking publicly.

vocab.meaning: showing an ability to accurately assess situations
